description: A white queen on b2 behind a white bishop on c3 on the long diagonal: both attack the black pawn on g7, the bishop directly and the queen as a battery through the bishop; the pawn is defended once, by the black king.
decisions: A queen forms a battery with a bishop on a diagonal and with a rook on a file or rank, because the queen moves along both kinds of line; a rook and a bishop never form one.
The front piece is the one nearer the covered squares; here the bishop on c3 is the front and the queen on b2 the back.
The king counts as a defender at L0 (count 1) but adds 0 to the summed value, so a square defended only by the king shows defence value 0.

A king defends a piece at L1 only if it could recapture there: the square is tested with the defended piece removed, and if any enemy piece then attacks it the defence is excluded with reason king_into_attack, naming every such enemy piece. Here the bishop attacks g7 directly once the pawn is gone and the queen attacks it through the bishop.
The battery line stops at the pawn on g7: neither piece attacks h8 beyond it.

assertions.note: The king could not recapture on g7: with the pawn gone the square is attacked by the bishop and, through it, the queen.
The bishop also defends its own king along c3-d2-e1.
